notes: Average 3.86 (4/4/4/4/4/3/4), the same as rc.2 and rc.3. Polish is still at 3, so the bar (avg >= 4.0) is not met. rc.4 was the extra iteration the user approved as the last one, so the loop stops here and goes to the user. This is the best round so far: all four big rc.3 polish defects are fixed. Polish stays at 3 because the 48px header drawings (one beside every h1) still fail the silhouette test in commerce and settings, and because of a few smaller defects listed below. The failures are now small and concentrated, not structural.

rc.3 issues, one by one. FIXED: (1) Wrong product. Every store card draws its own product: tote, backpack, duffel, sweater, tee, coat, mug, skillet, towels, key ring and beanie. The detail stage shows the same drawing (Canvas Field Tote is a tote; Merino Crew Sweater is a sweater). (2) Drawings adrift. Ink now spans about 45 to 55% of plates and stages (commerce detail tote ~47% of a 670px stage, blog featured ~45%). (3) Hands on plates and stages. The wrist strokes run off the plate's bottom edge and are clipped there, so the megaphone, flag, mug, towels and beanie plates read as hands, not creatures. (4) Stage sizing. The dashboard chart stage and settings plan stage hug their content (no dead lilac bands). At 390px the plans stack in source order, all fully visible, the current plan included. The dashboard keeps its chart stage on mobile. (5) Straight-edged subjects. No set square or ruler this round. (6) Banned defaults. No steaming mug as a screen subject (the Enamel Camp Mug is a product, which the spec exempts), no magnifier (the blog agent swapped its sieve for a funnel), no receipt, no envelope (the blog newsletter uses a mailbox), no mitten or sock. PARTIAL: (7) Hands as creatures. Fixed where a stage or plate clips the wrist. Not fixed on bare paper at size.pictoSm, where the wrist ends at the edge of an invisible box, so it still ends in the air (see Polish). (8) Block rise. The blog agent did not build it. Commerce, dashboard and settings built it, but all three report they temporarily disabled it to review screenshots, which the spec forbids ('never add overrides'). Captures are under reduced motion, so the gallery is unaffected. (9) Preview leftovers. None reported, so this is fixed. NOT APPLICABLE: the working glyph is still never visible, because no base app has a pending request (a harness gap, not penalised).

Polish 3, issue 1: header drawings at 48px fail the silhouette test, so the hand-at-pictoSm problem is still there. Commerce 'Shop all goods' (hang tag in hand) is an unreadable onion-like blob. Commerce 'Your cart' (basket in hand) reads as an acorn or pot, and it nearly matches the empty-cart paper bag drawn just below it. That breaks 'no two drawings in one app share a silhouette'. Settings 'Profile' (pen in hand) reads as a flame or a three-fingered hand. Settings 'Notifications' (bell in hand) reads as a small figure with legs. Settings 'Security' (key in hand) reads as a stick figure with a round head. Dashboard 'Overview' (stopwatch) carries a stray ':' to its left and an '=' under it. The dashboard agent reduced the hand to two flat lines 'coming in from the side', and at 48px they read as speed lines or a bug. 'Projects' (pennant) has the same flat-line '≡' hand. The mechanism: rc.4's wrist rule ('run off the box's bottom edge') only reads as a cut-off arm when something clips it. In a header the box edge is invisible paper, so the strokes still stop in mid-air under a round object, which reads as legs.

Polish 3, issue 2: drawings scaled up become heavy, broken marker lines. Stroke widths and the brush displacement are in viewBox units, so an 80% box on a 670px stage scales a 4.0 stroke to ~18px. On the commerce detail page the tote outline breaks into dash-like segments (the feDisplacementMap at that scale). On the blog featured and article stages the swatch-fan hand is drawn in ~16px strokes that look crude next to the 48px header drawings. The same family draws at two incompatible weights.

Polish 3, issue 3: article figures lie, the same class of error as rc.3's wrong product. The tests need a visible figure, and the spec says to omit figures without an image, so the blog agent filled each figure with an unrelated object on a lilac stage. 'The inventory board after grouping, forty-one buttons, six actual jobs' shows a push pin. 'The same release, described for the people who shipped it and for the people who use it' shows a rubber stamp. A reader expects the caption to describe the picture.

Polish, smaller items. (a) The blog uses color.stage.lake (#6a9bcc, a saturated mid-blue) as a plate. It is the loudest color in all four apps and breaks 'color is a whisper'. Commerce never uses it, so the plate palettes drift between apps. (b) The blog plate color follows grid position, not the post. 'Writing Release Notes' is lilac on home and lake in the article's related posts, and 'Running Calm Meetings' changes from lake to lilac. (c) Settings Billing gives 'Switch to Free' (a downgrade) the same ink primary as 'Switch to Business'. (d) Settings invoices: STATUS is squeezed against the right side, with ~170px of dead space after it. Revoke buttons sit 12px from the card's right edge against 24px on the left. (e) Dashboard header drawings have 10 frames; the recipe asks for 12 to 24.

Signature 4. All five elements are in all four apps and placed per Applying the concept. Blog: masthead accent drawing (notepad in hand, the one accent fill), a 4:3 sage drawing stage for the featured post, plates with each post's own drawing, a pictoMd prose opener (glasses) on About, a mailbox that swaps to a leaf on success. Commerce: header drawing, one drawing per product on plates, the same drawing on the 4:3 detail stage, empty cart on a lilac stage over a ghosted skeleton. Dashboard: header drawings on every screen, the chart in a raised card on a sage stage that shares edges with the activity card, breathing dots on Active. Settings: header drawings, plan cards with pictoMd drawings on a lilac stage, 'Active now' breathing. Motion frames confirm the strip, stepping once from frame 0, never blank, then holding: blog notepad 17 steps / 1411ms, mailbox 19 steps, commerce hang tag 17 steps, dashboard stopwatch 10 steps / 830ms, settings pen 17 steps. Header-in and lede rise-sm run. Held at 4, not 5, because of the 48px craft failures above, the 10-frame dashboard strip and the two stroke weights.

Cross-app 4. Clearly one family. The same paper and ink, a serif h1 beside a 48px drawing in the same header grid, 40px ring controls, stone chips with an ink selected chip, outline status badges with dots, 16px cards, a clay focus outline, warm dark mode, and dark pastel stages with off-white ink. Drift: the blog alone uses the lake plate; dashboard hands are flat lines while the other apps draw fingers; and plate stroke weight (blog, commerce) is double that of header drawings.

Hierarchy 4. Each screen leads with the serif h1 and its drawing, then one stage or main card. The store grid reads product-first, with the price clear. The dashboard puts its stats, then the chart on a stage, then the table. The billing downgrade-as-primary is the one exception (see the polish notes).

Spacing 4. Section gaps, the header padding and form rhythm match the scale across apps. Stage padding is space.48 on desktop and space.24 on mobile. Mobile stacked tables use the label grid. Minor: the dashboard stacks its four stat cards at 390px into ~900px of single cards (a 2x2 grid would hold), and the settings invoice columns are unbalanced.

States 4. Focus: the clay outline on search fields and controls in every app. Hover: linked cards get shadow.hover plus a title underline. Errors: danger ring, inline message, and 'N fields need attention' in commerce checkout, settings profile and password. Dialog: serif title, secondary plus primary actions. Filtered-empty states have a drawing, a serif title and one action (funnel in blog, binoculars in dashboard). Added to cart and Saved show a check-circle line; newsletter success swaps the drawing. Minor: the password strength hint lost its dot ('Strength: Strong' is bare green text).

Reference fidelity 4. Cream paper, warm ink, a serif display voice over a quiet sans, ink primary buttons, ringed secondary buttons, calm plan cards with small line drawings above the plan name, and bold brush drawings with an off-register fill. Anyone who knows the reference recognizes the character. Nothing is copied: no starburst, no reference copy or names.

Not counted: the sticky header painted mid-page and the dialog scrim ending at 900px in full-page state captures (harness artifacts), title-case post titles (test-pinned), and the invisible working glyph (harness gap).
promptFixes: Polish and signature, hands at size.pictoSm (spec gap; recipe step 1 and step 4). The wrist rule only works when a stage or plate clips the strokes. Add to step 4: 'At size.pictoSm and anywhere on bare paper (headers, empty states, openers, plan cards), draw the object alone, no hand. Hands appear only on plates and stages, where the clip edge makes the wrist read as an arm.' Change the hand quota in step 1 to 'at least half of each app's plate and stage drawings'. Add to Never: 'a hand on a drawing that is not clipped by a plate or stage edge; a hand reduced to straight lines'.

Signature, header silhouettes (strengthen step 4 and Verification). Add: 'Header drawings are the object's single most recognizable outline at 48px: a bell, a key, a tag with its hole and string, a basket with its handle arc. If two people would name it differently, choose another subject.' Add to Verification: 'Line up every header drawing and every empty-state drawing of one app at 48px; each must be nameable in one word and different from the others (a cart basket and an empty-cart bag are the same shape).'

Polish, stroke weight at large sizes (spec gap; pictogram CSS and Pastel stage). Add to the pictogram CSS: `.stage--drawing .picto path, .plate .picto path { stroke-width: calc(var(--w) * var(--picto-weight, 1)); }`, set `--picto-weight: 0.6` when the box is wider than 240px and `0.45` above 400px, and pass the brush filter `scale` through the same factor (1.6 on stages). Then state: 'A drawing's rendered line is 4 to 9px at every size; never thicker. Check the detail and featured stages at 1440px: no dashed or broken strokes.'

Polish, figures without images (spec gap; Layout adaptation, Article). Replace 'Figures without an image are omitted' with: 'A figure without an image, when it must stay (tests or layout), shows a ghosted preview of what its caption describes (raised cards at 60% opacity on a stage, laid out like the caption's board, list or comparison), never an unrelated object. If the caption cannot be drawn as a ghosted preview, shorten the figure to its caption in the article flow.' Add to Verification: 'Read every figure caption against its picture.'

Polish, lake plate (spec gap; Pastel stage colors). Change 'color.stage.lake only behind a card or drawing' to 'color.stage.lake only on hero stages behind a raised card; never on plates, drawing stages or grids. Plates rotate sage, lilac and apricot.' Add: 'A plate's color is chosen by the item (sum of its id's char codes mod 3), so the same post or product keeps its color on every screen; neighbors may then match, which is fine for plates.'

Hierarchy, plan actions (spec gap; Card plan variant). Add: 'On plan cards only the upgrade is ink primary. Downgrades and switches to a cheaper plan are secondary. The current plan shows its badge in the button row.'

Signature, frame count (agent mistake the spec already forbids; strengthen). Move '12 to 24 frames' into Verification: 'Every strip has 12 to 24 frames (count --n); a 6-stroke pictoSm drawing reaches 12 by repeating its last stroke frame and the 3 boil frames.'

Motion review overrides (agent mistake the spec already forbids; strengthen and move into the Never list). Three agents still disabled block rise to review screenshots. Add to Never: 'Disabling, overriding or removing any motion to review your work. Review with the browser's reduced-motion emulation, which already shows every block, frame and heading final.' Put the same sentence first in Verification's Reduced motion line.

Harness notes (not prompt fixes). (a) Add a capture state with a mocked 1s network response per base app, so the working glyph can be verified. (b) Full-page captures with motion allowed should scroll through the page first. (c) The blog base app needs figures with real images, or its tests should accept an omitted figure, so agents are not forced to invent figure art. (d) The settings base app's plan cards and the dashboard's placeholder Settings page differ in content; give the dashboard Settings page real content or drop it.
